Author: Kevin Galligan <kgalligan@gmail.com>
Date:   Sat Nov 14 16:47:35 2026 -0500

    Tips: an agent's export counts and brings the Tips window; a scratch instance counts no export (spec §11 TIP-3..TIP-5, TIP-7 amended, TIP-8)
    
    The owner overruled the first rule: an export over the agent socket, and
    the Assistant's, is real use. The `export` handler now follows its job as
    a queued export a person added is followed, so it counts, starts the 30
    days when it is the first, and the Tips window opens after it when the ask
    is due. The window is ordered front without taking key and is modal to
    nothing, so later calls answer.
    
    A proof's instance must still count nothing: an instance counts only when
    it runs from an app bundle and RC_AGENT_SOCKET is unset (TIP-8). Every
    proof launch of a real bundle sets it; nothing a person does sets it on
    the app. The dev-only -RCDevTipsSuite keeps the counting state in a
    throwaway suite for the live proof.
    
    Verified: make gate passes; tools/proof/tips_proof.py 40/40 on Debug and
    40/40 on Release, both on the final build; its nineteen mutants each
    caught on their named rows before the fix pass, and agent-unfollowed again
    after its anchor moved; with the Tips window up export_status,
    get_project, Settings… and a second export answered.
    
    Owed: the owner's manual checks CH-7..CH-10; make dist was not run; the
    app was in the background or probe-driven in the live rows, so an active
    app's key behaviour is CH-9 and CH-10.

     3	/// Settings' Tips pane (spec §11 TIP-6): the window's last. A bare heading,
     4	/// one visible sentence, the toggle and a Tips button.
     5	///
     6	/// **The toggle** (`TipsSettings`, on by default) decides two things at once:
     7	/// whether the editor shows its Tips button, and whether Frame Job ever shows
     8	/// the dialog by itself. It saves when it is pressed, with no Save button, and
     9	/// every open editor follows `TipsSettings.didChangeNotification`.
    10	///
    11	/// **The button is always there.** It shows the dialog whatever the toggle
    12	/// says, and is never hidden or disabled: with the toggle off it is the one
    13	/// way left to reach the dialog. What it shows is a parameter, so a probe
    14	/// presses it without a window appearing.
    15	///
    16	/// **No ⓘ.** The sentence is short enough to show (under SH-5's 200
    17	/// characters), and the dialog one press away says the rest. It is a
    18	/// person's setting: no tool reads or writes it (R6-12, MC-7).
    19	final class TipsSettingsPane: NSStackView {
    20	    static let paneTitle = "Tips"
    21	    static let blurb = "Frame Job is free and open source, made by one developer. Tips are voluntary."
    22	    static let toggleTitle = "Show the Tips button and the yearly reminder"
    23	    static let buttonTitle = "Tips"
    24	    /// The Settings window's width less its two insets.
    25	    private static let textWidth: CGFloat = 420
    26	
    27	    private let defaults: UserDefaults
    28	    private let showTips: () -> Void
    29	
    30	    let headingLabel = NSTextField(labelWithString: TipsSettingsPane.paneTitle)
    31	    let blurbLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: TipsSettingsPane.blurb)
    32	    let toggleBox = NSButton(
    33	        checkboxWithTitle: TipsSettingsPane.toggleTitle, target: nil, action: nil)
    34	    private(set) var tipsButton: NSButton!
    35	
    36	    init(defaults: UserDefaults, showTips: @escaping () -> Void) {
    37	        self.defaults = defaults
    38	        self.showTips = showTips
    39	        super.init(frame: .zero)
    40	        build()
    41	        sync()
    42	    }
    43	
    44	    @available(*, unavailable)
    45	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
    46	        fatalError("TipsSettingsPane does not support NSCoder")
    47	    }
    48	
    49	    private func build() {
    50	        headingLabel.font = DS.sans(15, weight: .bold)
    51	        headingLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
    52	        headingLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.tips.heading")
    53	
    54	        blurbLabel.font = DS.sans(13)
    55	        blurbLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
    56	        blurbLabel.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = Self.textWidth
    57	        blurbLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.tips.blurb")
    58	
    59	        toggleBox.font = DS.sans(13)
    60	        toggleBox.target = self
    61	        toggleBox.action = #selector(toggled(_:))
    62	        toggleBox.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.tips.toggle")
    63	
    64	        tipsButton = StickerButton(
    65	            title: Self.buttonTitle, style: .secondary, target: self,
    66	            action: #selector(tipsClicked(_:)))
    67	        tipsButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.tips.button")
    68	
    69	        orientation = .vertical
    70	        alignment = .leading
    71	        spacing = 12
    72	        for view in [headingLabel, blurbLabel, toggleBox, tipsButton] as [NSView] {
    73	            addArrangedSubview(view)
    74	        }
    75	    }
    76	
    77	    /// The stored toggle on the box. Reads only.
    78	    func sync() {
    79	        toggleBox.state = TipsSettings.isEnabled(in: defaults) ? .on : .off
    80	    }
    81	
    82	    @objc func toggled(_ sender: Any?) {
    83	        TipsSettings.setEnabled(toggleBox.state == .on, in: defaults)
    84	        sync()
    85	    }
    86	
    87	    @objc func tipsClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
    88	        showTips()
    89	    }

     3	/// The editor toolbar's Tips button (spec §11 TIP-6): green, right of
     4	/// Export…, showing the Tips dialog. **An experiment the owner may remove**:
     5	/// deleting this file and its one line in `buildToolbar` removes it.
     6	///
     7	/// A view around one `AccentButton` (which is final) so that it can hide
     8	/// ITSELF while Settings ▸ Tips' toggle is off and follow
     9	/// `TipsSettings.didChangeNotification`: the frozen editor file holds no
    10	/// property for it, and a hidden arranged subview leaves no gap in the
    11	/// toolbar's stack. The fill is `DS.tips`, a fixed green apart from the
    12	/// action ink in both appearances (CI-4). The press is the nil-target
    13	/// `showTips(_:)` on `AppDelegate`; it is not an edit, so it has no MCP
    14	/// mirror.
    15	final class TipsToolbarButton: NSView {
    16	    static let title = "Tips"
    17	    static let tooltip = "Support Frame Job"
    18	
    19	    private let defaults: UserDefaults
    20	    let button = AccentButton(
    21	        title: TipsToolbarButton.title, symbol: nil, fallback: "",
    22	        tooltip: TipsToolbarButton.tooltip, action: #selector(AppDelegate.showTips(_:)),
    23	        fill: DS.tips)
    24	
    25	    init(defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) {
    26	        self.defaults = defaults
    27	        super.init(frame: .zero)
    28	        button.setAccessibilityIdentifier("toolbar.tips")
    29	        button.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
    30	        addSubview(button)
    31	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
    32	            button.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: topAnchor),
    33	            button.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bottomAnchor),
    34	            button.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: leadingAnchor),
    35	            button.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: trailingAnchor),
    36	        ])
    37	        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
    38	            self, selector: #selector(settingsChanged(_:)),
    39	            name: TipsSettings.didChangeNotification, object: nil)
    40	        sync()
    41	    }
    42	
    43	    @available(*, unavailable)
    44	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
    45	        fatalError("TipsToolbarButton does not support NSCoder")
    46	    }
    47	
    48	    /// Shown exactly while the toggle is on.
    49	    func sync() {
    50	        isHidden = !TipsSettings.isEnabled(in: defaults)
    51	    }
    52	
    53	    @objc private func settingsChanged(_ note: Notification) {
    54	        sync()
    55	    }
    56	}

     1	import AppKit
     2	
     3	/// The Tips dialog (spec §11 TIP-1, TIP-2): who a tip funds, "Leave a Tip"
     4	/// and "Not Now".
     5	///
     6	/// **A window and not a sheet, deliberately.** It has three doors — the
     7	/// editor's Tips button, Settings' Tips button and the automatic ask — and
     8	/// two of them have no document to hold a sheet. It is modal to nothing, so
     9	/// no window and no tool call ever waits on it. `SettingsWindowController`'s
    10	/// mould: one instance, not released when closed, no frame autosave name.
    11	/// It is built from the sheets' own pieces so it reads as one of them, and
    12	/// it is left out of the Window menu because both buttons reopen it.
    13	///
    14	/// **Two ways to show it.** `show()` is a person's press: key and front, and
    15	/// it writes nothing. `showAutomatic()` is the ask Frame Job makes by itself
    16	/// (TIP-4): front WITHOUT key, so a Return typed into the editor can never
    17	/// press "Leave a Tip". The two order calls are closures because a probe's
    18	/// window is never key and could not tell the two apart otherwise.
    19	///
    20	/// **What "Leave a Tip" does.** Opens `TipsLink.url` in the browser, records
    21	/// the press as an ask (TIP-5) and closes. Nothing here knows whether anyone
    22	/// tipped.
    23	final class TipsWindowController: NSWindowController {
    24	    /// The app's one Tips dialog. A probe builds its own.
    25	    static let shared = TipsWindowController()
    26	
    27	    static let windowTitle = "Tips"
    28	    static let heading = "Frame Job is free and open source"
    29	    static let body =
    30	        "Frame Job is made by one developer. It is free to use and its source is open. If it "
    31	        + "is useful to you, a tip helps pay for the time to keep working on it. Tips are "
    32	        + "voluntary, and nothing in Frame Job is locked without one."
    33	    static let hint = "You can turn this reminder off in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Tips."
    34	    static let notNowTitle = "Not Now"
    35	    static let tipTitle = "Leave a Tip"
    36	
    37	    private let ask: TipsAsk
    38	    private let open: (URL) -> Void
    39	    private let orderKey: (NSWindow) -> Void
    40	    private let orderFront: (NSWindow) -> Void
    41	
    42	    private(set) var notNowButton: NSButton!
    43	    private(set) var tipButton: NSButton!
    44	
    45	    init(
    46	        ask: TipsAsk = .shared,
    47	        open: @escaping (URL) -> Void = { NSWorkspace.shared.open($0) },
    48	        orderKey: @escaping (NSWindow) -> Void = { $0.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil) },
    49	        orderFront: @escaping (NSWindow) -> Void = { $0.orderFront(nil) }
    50	    ) {
    51	        self.ask = ask
    52	        self.open = open
    53	        self.orderKey = orderKey
    54	        self.orderFront = orderFront
    55	        let window = NSWindow(
    56	            contentRect: NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: sheetWidth, height: 240),
    57	            styleMask: [.titled, .closable], backing: .buffered, defer: false)
    58	        window.title = Self.windowTitle
    59	        window.isReleasedWhenClosed = false
    60	        window.isExcludedFromWindowsMenu = true
    61	        super.init(window: window)
    62	        let content = buildContent()
    63	        window.contentView = content
    64	        window.setContentSize(content.fittingSize)
    65	        window.center()
    66	        applyBackground()
    67	    }
    68	
    69	    @available(*, unavailable)
    70	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
    71	        fatalError("TipsWindowController does not support NSCoder")
    72	    }
    73	
    74	    private func buildContent() -> NSView {
    75	        let width = sheetWidth - sheetInset * 2
    76	        let bodyLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: Self.body)
    77	        bodyLabel.font = DS.sans(13)
    78	        bodyLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
    79	        bodyLabel.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = width
    80	        bodyLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("tips.body")
    81	
    82	        let hintLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: Self.hint)
    83	        hintLabel.font = DS.sans(12)
    84	        hintLabel.textColor = DS.textMuted
    85	        hintLabel.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = width
    86	        hintLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("tips.hint")
    87	
    88	        notNowButton = StickerButton(
    89	            title: Self.notNowTitle, style: .secondary, target: self,
    90	            action: #selector(notNowClicked(_:)))
    91	        notNowButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("tips.notnow")
    92	        tipButton = StickerButton(
    93	            title: Self.tipTitle, style: .primary, target: self,
    94	            action: #selector(tipClicked(_:)))
    95	        tipButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("tips.tip")
    96	
    97	        return makeSheetView(
    98	            title: Self.heading, content: sheetColumn([bodyLabel, hintLabel]),
    99	            buttonRow: makeButtonRow(cancel: notNowButton, apply: tipButton))
   100	    }
   101	
   102	    private func applyBackground() {
   103	        window?.backgroundColor = DS.chromeBackground
   104	        window?.contentView?.layer?.backgroundColor = DS.chromeBackground.cgColor
   105	    }
   106	
   107	    // MARK: - Showing
   108	
   109	    /// A person's press of a Tips button: key and front. Writes nothing.
   110	    func show() {
   111	        guard let window else { return }
   112	        applyBackground()
   113	        orderKey(window)
   114	    }
   115	
   116	    /// The ask Frame Job makes by itself: front, never key (TIP-4).
   117	    func showAutomatic() {
   118	        guard let window else { return }
   119	        applyBackground()
   120	        orderFront(window)
   121	    }
   122	
   123	    // MARK: - Buttons
   124	
   125	    @objc func notNowClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
   126	        close()
   127	    }
   128	
   129	    @objc func tipClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
   130	        if let url = URL(string: TipsLink.url) { open(url) }
   131	        ask.noteTipPageOpened()
   132	        close()
   133	    }
   134	}
   135	
   136	// MARK: - The export doors
   137	
   138	/// The two places an export reaches Tips (TIP-4): the Export… sheet's success
   139	/// and a queued job, which is a person's Add to Queue
   140	/// (`EditorViewController+Export.swift`) or the agent's `export`
   141	/// (`AgentServer+Export.swift`, the Assistant's too). Both doors do nothing in
   142	/// a scratch instance (`counts`, TIP-8). The ask, the dialog, the queue and
   143	/// that rule are parameters so a probe runs the doors on its own. Main thread.
   144	final class TipsDoors {
   145	    static let shared = TipsDoors()
   146	
   147	    private let ask: TipsAsk
   148	    private let dialog: () -> TipsWindowController
   149	    private let queue: ExportQueueController
   150	    private let counts: () -> Bool
   151	    private var follower: TipsQueueFollower?
   152	    private var queueObserver: NSObjectProtocol?
   153	    /// The result sheets still up after a counted success, each waiting for
   154	    /// its window's sheet to end.
   155	    private var sheetEnds: [TipsSheetEnd] = []
   156	
   157	    init(
   158	        ask: TipsAsk = .shared,
   159	        dialog: @escaping () -> TipsWindowController = { TipsWindowController.shared },
   160	        queue: ExportQueueController = .shared,
   161	        counts: @escaping () -> Bool = { TipsInstance.isPersons }
   162	    ) {
   163	        self.ask = ask
   164	        self.dialog = dialog
   165	        self.queue = queue
   166	        self.counts = counts
   167	    }

    30	enum TipsSchedule {

    32	    static let firstAskExports = 5
    33	    static let skipMonths = 6
    34	
    35	    /// The Gregorian calendar in the Mac's time zone as it is now, whatever
    36	    /// calendar the person's Mac shows: "December" is its month 12.
    37	    static func localCalendar() -> Calendar {

    45	    /// December is due, and not one whose 1 December 00:00 is less than
    46	    /// `skipMonths` calendar months after the last ask.
    47	    static func isDue(_ state: TipsState, now: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> Bool {

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tips (spec §11 TIP-1…TIP-8) — the dialog, the editor's button, the automatic
ask, Settings' section, and whose exports count.

    python3 tools/proof/tips_proof.py [--only ROW,…] [--no-live] [--mutant NAME]

A plain run builds `tips_probe.swift` over `app/Sources` through
`swift_build.build` and runs it once (B0, S, A, F, I, C, W), reads the tree's
own text (T1), then drives four instances of the app `RC_PROOF_APP` chooses
over MCP (L). `--no-live` leaves the L rows out. Every string and number a
probe row compares is a literal in the probe. The probe is run with
`RC_AGENT_SOCKET` naming a path nothing binds, so I3 can read the process's
own environment.

The probe (no app, nothing on screen, no browser, no real defaults domain):

  B0   the probe builds.
  S1   nothing recorded, and five exports with no first export: not due.
  S2   five exports: 29 d 23 h after the first is not due, 30 d after (1 July)
       is.
  S3   four exports after 400 d is not due; five is.
  S4   the toggle off with everything else due: not due.
  S5   after an ask on 10 February: 15 July no, 30 November 23:59:59 no,
       1 December 00:00:00 yes, 31 December 23:59:59 yes, 1 January no.
  S6   a last ask at 1 June 00:00:00 leaves that December due; at 00:00:01 it
       does not; one on 20 August skips that December and not the next.
  S7   asked on 5 December: 20 December no, 2 December a year on yes.
  S8   one instant, 2027-11-30T12:00Z: due in Pacific/Auckland (1 December
       there), not in America/Los_Angeles.
  S9   a clock set back: a day before the first export, and a December before
       the last ask, are not due.
  S10  `TipsSchedule.localCalendar()` is Gregorian in the current time zone;
       the constants are 30, 5 and 6.
  A1   `countExport` twice: 1 then 2, the first export stamped once.
  A2   `takeAsk` is false and writes nothing before it is due; due, it is true
       once, writes last-asked as the clock, and is false at once after.
  A3   the toggle off: written as `FrameJobTips` false with one post;
       `takeAsk` false and nothing written; a sixth export still counts.
  A4   `noteTipPageOpened` writes last-asked alone.
  A5   the four key names; an absent toggle reads on; both dates are stored as
       dates; the link is `https://boppallewyn.com/frame-job/tips/`.
  F1   a followed job waiting, running, then completed: `completed` once over
       three settles.
  F2   a followed job cancelled, failed or removed: never, and dropped.
  F3   a completed job nobody followed: never; the followed one: once.
  I1   `TipsInstance.counts` with the app's bundle identifier: no variable
       counts; `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` a path does not; empty does; and
       `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` alone does, a relocated home being no condition.
  I2   no bundle identifier never counts, with or without the socket; the
       Debug bundle's identifier counts.
  I3   `TipsInstance.ofProcess` reads this process's own environment: handed
       a bundle with an identifier, made in the scratch folder, it is false
       (the proof set `RC_AGENT_SOCKET`) and true with an empty environment;
       the process as it is, and `TipsInstance.isPersons`, are false.
  C1   the dialog: its title, heading, body and hint; Not Now on Escape, Leave
       a Tip on Return; out of the Window menu, no frame autosave name;
       `show()` orders key and writes nothing; `showAutomatic()` orders front,
       never key; Not Now closes and writes nothing; Leave a Tip opens exactly
       the page, writes last-asked alone and closes. Its PNGs in both looks are
       written to `work/tips/…/scratch/` for a reader and checked for more
       than one colour only.
  C2   an in-process document's editor at 1440 pt and at the 900 pt minimum:
       the toolbar's row ends Export… then Tips; Tips is 12 pt after Export…
       and 12 pt from the edge, 26 pt tall at its own width; titled "Tips",
       fill #2E7D32, a nil-target `showTips:`, its tooltip; at 900 pt every
       control keeps its 1440 pt width and the spacer is wider than 0.
  C3   the toggle off (the argument domain, then the notification): the button
       is hidden and Export… is 12 pt from the edge; on again: back.
  C4   Settings' pane: heading, blurb, toggle, button; the literals; on by
       default; no info button; unticking writes `FrameJobTips` false and
       posts once; the Tips button is there, enabled, and shows the dialog in
       both states; the pane writes one key.
  W2   Export… through `EditorViewController.beginExport` on a state one
       export short of due: an export to a folder that is not there fails, and
       a cancelled one dismisses its sheet; neither counts, asks or orders the
       dialog.
  W1   the same door, a success: counted while the result sheet is still up,
       not asked; after Close the dialog is ordered front (never key) and
       last-asked is recorded; a second export counts and does not ask.
  W3   Add to Queue's door (`TipsDoors.follow`) on the probe's own queue: a
       job nobody followed and a followed one both complete, a followed third
       is cancelled while it waits; exactly one export is counted and the
       dialog is ordered front once.
  W4   the agent's door, `AgentServer.exportProject(_:tips:)`, on a registered
       in-process document and the shared queue, in a person's instance
       (`counts` true): the call answers an id and `export_status` reaches
       `done`; counted (5 from 4); ordered front, never key, last-asked
       recorded; no modal session was run (the probe's watchdog saw none and
       `NSApp.modalWindow` is nil); with the dialog shown `export_status`
       still answers and a second `export` reaches `done`, counted (6) and
       not asked again.
  W5   the same door in a scratch instance (`counts` false): the export
       reaches `done`; the store is exactly its seed and nothing is ordered.
  W6   the Export… door in a scratch instance: a success and Close; the same.
  W7   the agent's door with `TipsDoors`' DEFAULT rule, in this process (a
       scratch instance): the export reaches `done`; the store is exactly its
       seed and nothing is ordered.

The tree's text, read from the same sources the probe was built from:

  T1   `.exportSucceeded(` is called once, in `EditorViewController+Export.swift`;
       `.follow(queueJob:` is called twice, once there and once in
       `AgentServer+Export.swift`; `TipsDoors` is named in those two files and
       `TipsWindowController.swift` alone; `.takeAsk(` and `.countExport(` are
       called in `TipsWindowController.swift` alone; `RCDevTipsSuite` is
       spelled in `Tips.swift` alone.

The app over MCP (`mcp.launch`, each instance stopped by its own pid):

  L0   `grep "Frame Job: "` of each instance's log prints nothing.
  L1   launched with `-FrameJobTips YES`: the toolbar capture's layout dump has
       a visible view reading "Tips" (`toolbar.tips`) right of the one reading
       "Export…"; the PNG is not one colour.
  L2   the same instance, which is a proof's (a scratch socket, TIP-8): an
       agent `export` of a one-clip project reaches `done`; `snapshot_ui`'s
       listing has no window titled "Tips" and `mcp.defaults_moved` is empty.
  L3   launched with `-FrameJobTips NO`: no visible view of the toolbar reads
       "Tips"; Settings' dump has the visible "Tips" button
       (`settings.tips.button`) and the toggle's title.
  L4   launched with `-RCDevTipsSuite <suite>` (TIP-7), the suite a throwaway
       `framejob.tips-proof.…` domain seeded with 4 exports and a first export
       40 days back: an agent `export` reaches `done`; the suite then reads 5
       exports and a last-asked date inside the run; the listing has one
       visible window titled "Tips" that is not key; `get_project` answers
       within 15 s, Frame Job ▸ Settings… is performed (nothing is app-modal)
       and a second `export` reaches `done`, the suite reading 6 with
       last-asked unchanged; `mcp.defaults_moved` is empty. Whether the app
       was active is printed, not held. After the instance stops,
       `proof_defaults.remove_domain` removes the suite.
  L5   launched with a second suite and `-RCDevDerivedHidden YES`:
       `new_project_from_range` makes a document with no window, its source
       is closed and the listing has no editor window; the windowless
       document's `export` reaches `done`, the suite reads 5 and a last-asked
       date, the listing has the visible "Tips" window, and `get_project`
       answers within 15 s. Whether the window is key is printed, not held:
       an active app with no other window may hand it key. The suite is
       removed afterwards.

1	# Spec §11 — decisions: Tips
     2	
     3	Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
     4	[`README.md`](README.md).
     5	
     6	These were made with no road map, from the owner's words of 2026-11-14: a tips dialog, a green
     7	Tips button to the right of Export in the editor, an automatic ask on a usage-then-calendar
     8	schedule, and a Settings section that turns the ask and the button off. The owner called the
     9	button an experiment that may be removed. The same day, having seen it built, the owner overruled
    10	one part: "Exports over the MCP count. That user is getting value from the app, and getting
    11	something that other video apps don't really offer. Assuming the dialog doesn't prevent further
    12	MCP calls, the dialog should open." TIP-3, TIP-4, TIP-5 and TIP-7 are amended in place for it,
    13	each saying what changed, and TIP-8 is new.
    14	
    15	- **TIP-1 — A tip is voluntary, nothing in Frame Job is gated on one, and the app holds no payment
    16	  code: the dialog says who a tip funds and opens one web page.** The statement is plain: Frame
    17	  Job is made by one developer, it is free to use and its source is open, a tip helps pay for the
    18	  time to keep working on it, and nothing is locked without one. "Leave a Tip" opens
    19	  `https://boppallewyn.com/frame-job/tips/` in the person's browser, and that address is ONE
    20	  constant (`TipsLink.url`, `Tips.swift`), so moving the page is a one-line change. The page is
    21	  the owner's to make. Frame Job never learns whether anyone tipped, so there is no "thank you"
    22	  state and nothing to restore. Risk accepted: until the page exists the button opens a missing
    23	  page.
    24	- **TIP-2 — The dialog is its own small window titled "Tips", not a sheet and not an app-modal
    25	  alert, and it has three doors: the editor's Tips button, Settings' Tips button and the automatic
    26	  ask.** A sheet needs a host window and two of the doors have no document (Settings, and Settings
    27	  opened from the Welcome window); an app-modal alert would stop every window and would sit in
    28	  front of an MCP client's calls. A window that is modal to nothing cannot make anything wait. It
    29	  is the Settings window's mould (`TipsWindowController`): one instance, not released when closed,
    30	  no frame autosave name (so it writes no `NSWindow Frame` key), built from the sheets' own pieces
    31	  (`makeSheetView`, `makeButtonRow`) so it reads as one of them, Escape on "Not Now" and Return on
    32	  "Leave a Tip". It is left out of the Window menu: a two-button dialog is not a place to come
    33	  back to, and both buttons reopen it. There is no menu item for it, and no MCP mirror, because
    34	  showing it is not an edit (spec §7.9).
    35	- **TIP-3 — The automatic ask is due by usage first and the calendar after: never while the
    36	  toggle is off; first once at least 5 exports are counted AND at least 30 × 24 hours have passed
    37	  since the first counted export; after an ask, only in a December, and a December is skipped
    38	  whole when its 1 December 00:00 is less than six calendar months after the last ask.** The rule
    39	  is one pure function, `TipsSchedule.isDue(_:now:calendar:)`, over the stored state, the moment
    40	  and a calendar. "30 days of use" counts from the first counted export and not from the first
    41	  launch: a launch is also what every proof makes, and a copy that was opened and never exported
    42	  from has not been used (amended 2026-11-14 with TIP-4: this read "a date stamped at launch
    43	  would count use by agents alone", and an agent's export is use now). It is elapsed time, not
    44	  thirty separate days of use, which would make an occasional user wait a year. "December" is month 12 of the GREGORIAN calendar in
    45	  the Mac's current time zone (`TipsSchedule.localCalendar()`, built at each evaluation), whatever
    46	  calendar the person's Mac shows, so the same instant can be December in Auckland and November
    47	  in Los Angeles. A December is judged whole so that an ask on 30 June cannot bring the next one
    48	  on 30 December: a last ask after 1 June 00:00 skips that year's December, and one at or before
    49	  it does not. A clock set back before the last ask or the first export makes nothing due. Risk
    50	  accepted: the rule is evaluated only when a counted export completes (TIP-4), so a person who
    51	  exports nothing in December is not asked that year.
    52	- **TIP-4 — Every export that completes in a person's instance (TIP-8) counts, whoever started
    53	  it, and its completion evaluates the ask: the export card's two commits, an MCP client's
    54	  `export` and the Assistant's `export` (amended 2026-11-14, the owner: "Exports over the MCP
    55	  count").** Before the amendment only an export a person confirmed in the export card counted,
    56	  the agent's `export` was never followed, and an instance driven only by an agent was never
    57	  shown the dialog; the owner overruled that because a person whose agent exports for them is
    58	  using Frame Job, and in a way other editors do not offer. The card's two commits are Export…
    59	  (`EditorViewController.beginExport`), which hands the progress sheet an `onSuccess` it calls
    60	  once, on a success only, and Add to Queue (`enqueueExport`), which follows its job by the id
    61	  `enqueue` answered (`TipsQueueFollower`, `AgentExports`' pattern). The agent's `export`
    62	  (`AgentServer.exportProject`) enqueues on the same queue and follows its job through the same
    63	  `TipsDoors.follow(queueJob:)`, and the Assistant tab's `export` is that same handler, so there
    64	  is one line for both callers, `ExportQueueController` is not changed and its jobs carry no
    65	  origin. A counted export is counted when it succeeds; a cancel, a failure and a call the tool
    66	  refused count nothing. The ask is evaluated, and recorded, at the moment it is shown: for
    67	  Export…, when the result sheet ends (Close or Show in Finder), one main-queue turn later; for a
    68	  queued job, a person's or an agent's, when it completes. The automatic ask is ordered front
    69	  WITHOUT becoming key, so a Return typed into the editor can never press "Leave a Tip"; the two
    70	  buttons' doors make it key. **It never makes a tool call wait:** the window is modal to nothing
    71	  (TIP-2) and a queued job's ask runs from the queue's own notification, outside every call and
    72	  outside the agent lane's lock, so `export_status`, the next `export` and every other tool
    73	  answer as they did. What keeps a proof's exports from counting is not the door any more but
    74	  the instance (TIP-8). Risks accepted: after Show in Finder the dialog appears behind Finder and
    75	  is found on return; a window closed with its result sheet still attached never ends that
    76	  sheet, so that export is counted and the ask waits for the next one; Frame Job is usually in
    77	  the background when an agent's export ends, so the dialog waits there without bringing Frame
    78	  Job forward, and when the person comes back it may be the window that becomes key, where
    79	  Return is "Leave a Tip"; a client that exports in a loop is asked once, at the export that
    80	  made it due.
    81	- **TIP-5 — The state is four keys of the bundle's defaults domain, and no export in a scratch
    82	  instance writes one (TIP-8): an export writes only when it succeeds in a person's instance,
    83	  whoever started it, and the dialog's and Settings' own controls write wherever a person
    84	  presses them (amended 2026-11-14 with TIP-4: this read "written only at a person's
    85	  doors").** Only the two export doors ask TIP-8's rule; "Leave a Tip" and Settings' checkbox
    86	  do not, being presses no tool can make. `FrameJobTips` (Bool, absent means on) is the toggle, written by Settings' checkbox.
    87	  `FrameJobTipsExports` (Int) and `FrameJobTipsFirstExport` (a date, stamped once) are written
    88	  when a counted export succeeds, and counting goes on while the toggle is off, so turning it back
    89	  on behaves sensibly. `FrameJobTipsLastAsked` (a date) is written when the automatic ask is shown
    90	  and when "Leave a Tip" is pressed from any door: someone who has just visited the page is not
    91	  asked again that December. Opening the dialog by hand and choosing "Not Now", or closing it,
    92	  writes nothing. Dates are stored as dates, so `defaults write … -date` sets one. No project
    93	  format changes. Risk accepted: the state is per Mac and per build identity, so a Debug build
    94	  and a reinstall on another Mac each start again.
    95	- **TIP-6 — The editor's Tips button is an `AccentButton` filled with `DS.tips` (`#2E7D32`), right
    96	  of Export…, and Settings ▸ Tips holds the toggle that removes it.** The owner asked for green.
    97	  The fill is a fixed leaf green, the same in both appearances as the recorder's coral Record
    98	  button is, with the white `DS.onAccent` label at 5.1:1. It is deliberately not `DS.action` and
    99	  not `DS.forest`: CI-4 keeps mint for the action ink and nothing else, and forest (`#1F8564`) is
   100	  within 10/255 of the action ink's light value (`#1E8F6E`), so a forest button would read as an
   101	  action in the light appearance. `DS.tips` sits about 40° of hue from both action values, so
   102	  CI-4 stands unamended. How it looks is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`. The button is 12 pt
   103	  after Export… with no rule between them, has no symbol, and is `TipsToolbarButton`, a view that
   104	  hides itself while the toggle is off and follows `TipsSettings.didChangeNotification`, so the
   105	  frozen editor file holds nothing for it: removing the experiment is deleting that file and one
   106	  line of `buildToolbar`. Settings' fifth and last pane, "Tips", is a bare heading, one visible
   107	  sentence (under SH-5's and `settings_layout_probe` L5's 200 characters, so it needs no ⓘ), the
   108	  checkbox "Show the Tips button and the yearly reminder" (on by default) and a "Tips" button.
   109	  Unticking stops the automatic ask and removes the button from every open editor at once; the
   110	  pane's own button is never hidden or disabled and shows the dialog whatever the toggle says. It
   111	  is a person's setting: no tool reads or writes it (R6-12, MC-7).
   112	- **TIP-7 — The feature has one `-RCDev` switch, `-RCDevTipsSuite <name>`, and no dev tool; its
   113	  proof is a probe and, for what only the running app can show, four instances over MCP
   114	  (amended 2026-11-14 with TIP-4: this read "no `-RCDev` switch", and the mutants were twelve).**
   115	  `tools/proof/tips_proof.py` builds `tips_probe.swift` over `app/Sources` and hands the schedule
   116	  its clock, calendar and a scratch defaults store; the export doors are run for real, on a
   117	  document made in process, with the ask, the window, the queue and the instance rule injected
   118	  (`TipsDoors`), the agent's among them through `AgentServer.exportProject(_:tips:)`, and the
   119	  window's two order calls are closures so "front, not key" can be read where no probe window is
   120	  ever key. A person pins state with `defaults write` (`docs/manual-checks.md`). **The switch**
   121	  exists because a counted agent export on the running app, with the window really ordered and
   122	  the next call really answered, cannot be seen without writing some defaults domain, and it
   123	  must not be the bundle's: under `-RCDevTipsSuite <name>` (a build with the dev tools only, so
   124	  never Distribution) the three counting keys are read and written in the named suite and the
   125	  instance counts whatever its socket (TIP-8). One switch does both on purpose, so counting can
   126	  never be turned on in a proof's instance while the state is still the bundle's. The name must
   127	  start with `framejob.`, the prefix `proof_defaults.py` owns and removes; any other name, or a
   128	  suite that cannot be made, is named on stderr and ignored whole, and the instance stays as
   129	  TIP-8 judged it. It has no `dist_check.py` row: it widens nothing a person could reach, and
   130	  the seam's own needle (D1–D5) is what proves dev code is out of Distribution. The offscreen
   131	  harness pins `FrameJobTips` OFF: older chrome proofs read the toolbar at fixed points
   132	  (`sharp_chrome.py`'s `EXPORT_RIGHT`, `phase7_chrome.py`'s accent patch) and a button right of
   133	  Export… would move them; `screens.py` pins it ON, the first-run state the catalog shows, and
   134	  lists the other three keys and the switch in `NOT_SHOWN`. The proof's live instances launch
   135	  with `-FrameJobTips YES` or `NO`, so the owner's own toggle never decides a row. It holds
   136	  nineteen mutants, nine past the usual ten, because the feature holds nineteen separable
   137	  decisions and dropping one would leave a decision no row is seen failing for: the first
   138	  eleven of the original twelve (two thresholds, the toggle, the month, the skip, the recorded
   139	  ask, which queue states count, the button's and the pane's halves of the toggle, the success
   140	  wiring and the order call; the twelfth, "the agent's door follows", guarded the decision TIP-4
   141	  reversed and is gone), and eight for the amendment: the agent's door following its job, the
   142	  two conditions of TIP-8, the process's own environment being what is judged, the rule being
   143	  the doors' default, each of the two doors asking it, and the ask running no modal session. A
   144	  mutant is a probe rebuild and never runs a row against the app, so none can write a real
   145	  domain.
   146	- **TIP-8 — A scratch instance counts nothing and asks nothing, from any door: an instance is a
   147	  person's only when it runs from an app bundle and `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` is unset or empty.** The
   148	  reason TIP-4 first excluded the agent's door still stands for the proofs: they export over MCP
   149	  constantly and share the bundle's defaults domain, the owner's real one for a Release proof
   150	  (#238), so they must not count, must not move the owner's Tips state, must not trip `mcp.py`'s
   151	  `DEFAULTS MOVED` guard and must not put a Tips window into a capture. The rule is one pure
   152	  function, `TipsInstance.counts(environment:bundleIdentifier:)`, read once for the process
   153	  (`TipsInstance.isPersons`) and asked by both of `TipsDoors`' doors before anything is followed,
   154	  counted or asked, so it is a rule about the instance and not about who started the export.
   155	  **The socket variable** is the mark of a proof's instance because it cannot be forgotten: MC-6
   156	  keeps every proof off the person's socket, so an instance a proof can reach is one it gave
   157	  `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` (`mcp.launch` sets it on every launch, and every proof that starts the app
   158	  itself does), and the helper already calls that a scratch instance and launches it differently
   159	  (`mcp-proxy/src/launch.rs`). Empty reads as unset, as `AgentServer.socketPlan` reads it.
   160	  Nothing a person does sets it by accident: Copy MCP Command writes no environment, and the
   161	  helper passes the variable to the app only when its own environment holds it, which the site
   162	  documents as testing a second copy. **The bundle** is the mark of a probe or the harness,
   163	  which run the app's code in a bare executable with no bundle identifier and so count nothing
   164	  even when they reach a door in process (`assistant_lane_probe.swift` submits `export`). It is a
   165	  product rule and not a `-RCDev` switch: Distribution judges itself the same way, where it
   166	  means a test copy on its own socket is not counted. A relocated home (`CFFIXED_USER_HOME`) is
   167	  deliberately NOT a condition: macOS sets it in sandboxed processes, `open` hands an app its
   168	  caller's environment, so a person whose MCP client is sandboxed would silently never be
   169	  counted, and no proof needs it, since every proof launch of a real bundle that sets the home
   170	  sets the socket too. The loud backstop is unchanged: a proof instance that did count would
   171	  write `FrameJobTipsExports`, and `mcp.py`'s guard ends that script with status 3. Risks
   172	  accepted: a person who runs their everyday copy with `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` set is never counted or
   173	  asked, not even for an Export… of their own in that copy; a probe built as a bundle with an
   174	  identifier of its own would count into its own domain, never the app's, if it ever ran a door.

    29	  is the Settings window's mould (`TipsWindowController`): one instance, not released when closed,
    30	  no frame autosave name (so it writes no `NSWindow Frame` key), built from the sheets' own pieces
    31	  (`makeSheetView`, `makeButtonRow`) so it reads as one of them, Escape on "Not Now" and Return on
    32	  "Leave a Tip". It is left out of the Window menu: a two-button dialog is not a place to come
    33	  back to, and both buttons reopen it. There is no menu item for it, and no MCP mirror, because
    34	  showing it is not an edit (spec §7.9).
    35	- **TIP-3 — The automatic ask is due by usage first and the calendar after: never while the
    36	  toggle is off; first once at least 5 exports are counted AND at least 30 × 24 hours have passed
    37	  since the first counted export; after an ask, only in a December, and a December is skipped
    38	  whole when its 1 December 00:00 is less than six calendar months after the last ask.** The rule
    39	  is one pure function, `TipsSchedule.isDue(_:now:calendar:)`, over the stored state, the moment
    40	  and a calendar. "30 days of use" counts from the first counted export and not from the first
    41	  launch: a launch is also what every proof makes, and a copy that was opened and never exported
    42	  from has not been used (amended 2026-11-14 with TIP-4: this read "a date stamped at launch
    43	  would count use by agents alone", and an agent's export is use now). It is elapsed time, not
    44	  thirty separate days of use, which would make an occasional user wait a year. "December" is month 12 of the GREGORIAN calendar in
    45	  the Mac's current time zone (`TipsSchedule.localCalendar()`, built at each evaluation), whatever
    46	  calendar the person's Mac shows, so the same instant can be December in Auckland and November
    47	  in Los Angeles. A December is judged whole so that an ask on 30 June cannot bring the next one
    48	  on 30 December: a last ask after 1 June 00:00 skips that year's December, and one at or before
    49	  it does not. A clock set back before the last ask or the first export makes nothing due. Risk
    50	  accepted: the rule is evaluated only when a counted export completes (TIP-4), so a person who
    51	  exports nothing in December is not asked that year.
    52	- **TIP-4 — Every export that completes in a person's instance (TIP-8) counts, whoever started
    53	  it, and its completion evaluates the ask: the export card's two commits, an MCP client's
    54	  `export` and the Assistant's `export` (amended 2026-11-14, the owner: "Exports over the MCP
    55	  count").** Before the amendment only an export a person confirmed in the export card counted,
    56	  the agent's `export` was never followed, and an instance driven only by an agent was never
    57	  shown the dialog; the owner overruled that because a person whose agent exports for them is
    58	  using Frame Job, and in a way other editors do not offer. The card's two commits are Export…
    59	  (`EditorViewController.beginExport`), which hands the progress sheet an `onSuccess` it calls
    60	  once, on a success only, and Add to Queue (`enqueueExport`), which follows its job by the id
    61	  `enqueue` answered (`TipsQueueFollower`, `AgentExports`' pattern). The agent's `export`
    62	  (`AgentServer.exportProject`) enqueues on the same queue and follows its job through the same
    63	  `TipsDoors.follow(queueJob:)`, and the Assistant tab's `export` is that same handler, so there
    64	  is one line for both callers, `ExportQueueController` is not changed and its jobs carry no
    65	  origin. A counted export is counted when it succeeds; a cancel, a failure and a call the tool
    66	  refused count nothing. The ask is evaluated, and recorded, at the moment it is shown: for
    67	  Export…, when the result sheet ends (Close or Show in Finder), one main-queue turn later; for a
    68	  queued job, a person's or an agent's, when it completes. The automatic ask is ordered front
    69	  WITHOUT becoming key, so a Return typed into the editor can never press "Leave a Tip"; the two
    70	  buttons' doors make it key. **It never makes a tool call wait:** the window is modal to nothing
    71	  (TIP-2) and a queued job's ask runs from the queue's own notification, outside every call and
    72	  outside the agent lane's lock, so `export_status`, the next `export` and every other tool
    73	  answer as they did. What keeps a proof's exports from counting is not the door any more but
    74	  the instance (TIP-8). Risks accepted: after Show in Finder the dialog appears behind Finder and
    75	  is found on return; a window closed with its result sheet still attached never ends that
    76	  sheet, so that export is counted and the ask waits for the next one; Frame Job is usually in
    77	  the background when an agent's export ends, so the dialog waits there without bringing Frame
    78	  Job forward, and when the person comes back it may be the window that becomes key, where
    79	  Return is "Leave a Tip"; a client that exports in a loop is asked once, at the export that
    80	  made it due.
    81	- **TIP-5 — The state is four keys of the bundle's defaults domain, and no export in a scratch
    82	  instance writes one (TIP-8): an export writes only when it succeeds in a person's instance,
    83	  whoever started it, and the dialog's and Settings' own controls write wherever a person
    84	  presses them (amended 2026-11-14 with TIP-4: this read "written only at a person's
    85	  doors").** Only the two export doors ask TIP-8's rule; "Leave a Tip" and Settings' checkbox
    86	  do not, being presses no tool can make. `FrameJobTips` (Bool, absent means on) is the toggle, written by Settings' checkbox.
    87	  `FrameJobTipsExports` (Int) and `FrameJobTipsFirstExport` (a date, stamped once) are written
    88	  when a counted export succeeds, and counting goes on while the toggle is off, so turning it back
    89	  on behaves sensibly. `FrameJobTipsLastAsked` (a date) is written when the automatic ask is shown
    90	  and when "Leave a Tip" is pressed from any door: someone who has just visited the page is not
    91	  asked again that December. Opening the dialog by hand and choosing "Not Now", or closing it,
    92	  writes nothing. Dates are stored as dates, so `defaults write … -date` sets one. No project
    93	  format changes. Risk accepted: the state is per Mac and per build identity, so a Debug build
    94	  and a reinstall on another Mac each start again.
    95	- **TIP-6 — The editor's Tips button is an `AccentButton` filled with `DS.tips` (`#2E7D32`), right
    96	  of Export…, and Settings ▸ Tips holds the toggle that removes it.** The owner asked for green.
    97	  The fill is a fixed leaf green, the same in both appearances as the recorder's coral Record
    98	  button is, with the white `DS.onAccent` label at 5.1:1. It is deliberately not `DS.action` and
    99	  not `DS.forest`: CI-4 keeps mint for the action ink and nothing else, and forest (`#1F8564`) is
   100	  within 10/255 of the action ink's light value (`#1E8F6E`), so a forest button would read as an
   101	  action in the light appearance. `DS.tips` sits about 40° of hue from both action values, so
   102	  CI-4 stands unamended. How it looks is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`. The button is 12 pt
   103	  after Export… with no rule between them, has no symbol, and is `TipsToolbarButton`, a view that
   104	  hides itself while the toggle is off and follows `TipsSettings.didChangeNotification`, so the
   105	  frozen editor file holds nothing for it: removing the experiment is deleting that file and one
   106	  line of `buildToolbar`. Settings' fifth and last pane, "Tips", is a bare heading, one visible
   107	  sentence (under SH-5's and `settings_layout_probe` L5's 200 characters, so it needs no ⓘ), the
   108	  checkbox "Show the Tips button and the yearly reminder" (on by default) and a "Tips" button.
   109	  Unticking stops the automatic ask and removes the button from every open editor at once; the
   110	  pane's own button is never hidden or disabled and shows the dialog whatever the toggle says. It
   111	  is a person's setting: no tool reads or writes it (R6-12, MC-7).
   112	- **TIP-7 — The feature has one `-RCDev` switch, `-RCDevTipsSuite <name>`, and no dev tool; its
   113	  proof is a probe and, for what only the running app can show, four instances over MCP
   114	  (amended 2026-11-14 with TIP-4: this read "no `-RCDev` switch", and the mutants were twelve).**
   115	  `tools/proof/tips_proof.py` builds `tips_probe.swift` over `app/Sources` and hands the schedule
   116	  its clock, calendar and a scratch defaults store; the export doors are run for real, on a
   117	  document made in process, with the ask, the window, the queue and the instance rule injected
   118	  (`TipsDoors`), the agent's among them through `AgentServer.exportProject(_:tips:)`, and the
   119	  window's two order calls are closures so "front, not key" can be read where no probe window is
   120	  ever key. A person pins state with `defaults write` (`docs/manual-checks.md`). **The switch**
   121	  exists because a counted agent export on the running app, with the window really ordered and
   122	  the next call really answered, cannot be seen without writing some defaults domain, and it
   123	  must not be the bundle's: under `-RCDevTipsSuite <name>` (a build with the dev tools only, so
   124	  never Distribution) the three counting keys are read and written in the named suite and the
   125	  instance counts whatever its socket (TIP-8). One switch does both on purpose, so counting can
   126	  never be turned on in a proof's instance while the state is still the bundle's. The name must
   127	  start with `framejob.`, the prefix `proof_defaults.py` owns and removes; any other name, or a
   128	  suite that cannot be made, is named on stderr and ignored whole, and the instance stays as
   129	  TIP-8 judged it. It has no `dist_check.py` row: it widens nothing a person could reach, and
   130	  the seam's own needle (D1–D5) is what proves dev code is out of Distribution. The offscreen
   131	  harness pins `FrameJobTips` OFF: older chrome proofs read the toolbar at fixed points
   132	  (`sharp_chrome.py`'s `EXPORT_RIGHT`, `phase7_chrome.py`'s accent patch) and a button right of
   133	  Export… would move them; `screens.py` pins it ON, the first-run state the catalog shows, and
   134	  lists the other three keys and the switch in `NOT_SHOWN`. The proof's live instances launch
   135	  with `-FrameJobTips YES` or `NO`, so the owner's own toggle never decides a row. It holds
   136	  nineteen mutants, nine past the usual ten, because the feature holds nineteen separable
   137	  decisions and dropping one would leave a decision no row is seen failing for: the first
   138	  eleven of the original twelve (two thresholds, the toggle, the month, the skip, the recorded
   139	  ask, which queue states count, the button's and the pane's halves of the toggle, the success
   140	  wiring and the order call; the twelfth, "the agent's door follows", guarded the decision TIP-4
   141	  reversed and is gone), and eight for the amendment: the agent's door following its job, the
   142	  two conditions of TIP-8, the process's own environment being what is judged, the rule being
   143	  the doors' default, each of the two doors asking it, and the ask running no modal session. A
   144	  mutant is a probe rebuild and never runs a row against the app, so none can write a real
   145	  domain.
   146	- **TIP-8 — A scratch instance counts nothing and asks nothing, from any door: an instance is a
   147	  person's only when it runs from an app bundle and `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` is unset or empty.** The
   148	  reason TIP-4 first excluded the agent's door still stands for the proofs: they export over MCP
   149	  constantly and share the bundle's defaults domain, the owner's real one for a Release proof
   150	  (#238), so they must not count, must not move the owner's Tips state, must not trip `mcp.py`'s
   151	  `DEFAULTS MOVED` guard and must not put a Tips window into a capture. The rule is one pure
   152	  function, `TipsInstance.counts(environment:bundleIdentifier:)`, read once for the process
   153	  (`TipsInstance.isPersons`) and asked by both of `TipsDoors`' doors before anything is followed,
   154	  counted or asked, so it is a rule about the instance and not about who started the export.
   155	  **The socket variable** is the mark of a proof's instance because it cannot be forgotten: MC-6
   156	  keeps every proof off the person's socket, so an instance a proof can reach is one it gave
   157	  `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` (`mcp.launch` sets it on every launch, and every proof that starts the app
   158	  itself does), and the helper already calls that a scratch instance and launches it differently
   159	  (`mcp-proxy/src/launch.rs`). Empty reads as unset, as `AgentServer.socketPlan` reads it.
   160	  Nothing a person does sets it by accident: Copy MCP Command writes no environment, and the
   161	  helper passes the variable to the app only when its own environment holds it, which the site
   162	  documents as testing a second copy. **The bundle** is the mark of a probe or the harness,
   163	  which run the app's code in a bare executable with no bundle identifier and so count nothing
   164	  even when they reach a door in process (`assistant_lane_probe.swift` submits `export`). It is a
   165	  product rule and not a `-RCDev` switch: Distribution judges itself the same way, where it
   166	  means a test copy on its own socket is not counted. A relocated home (`CFFIXED_USER_HOME`) is
   167	  deliberately NOT a condition: macOS sets it in sandboxed processes, `open` hands an app its
   168	  caller's environment, so a person whose MCP client is sandboxed would silently never be
   169	  counted, and no proof needs it, since every proof launch of a real bundle that sets the home
   170	  sets the socket too. The loud backstop is unchanged: a proof instance that did count would
   171	  write `FrameJobTipsExports`, and `mcp.py`'s guard ends that script with status 3. Risks
   172	  accepted: a person who runs their everyday copy with `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` set is never counted or
   173	  asked, not even for an Export… of their own in that copy; a probe built as a bundle with an
   174	  identifier of its own would count into its own domain, never the app's, if it ever ran a door.

1	---
     2	title: Tips
     3	description: What a tip pays for, where the Tips button is, when Frame Job asks by itself, and how to turn both off.
     4	---
     5	
     6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
     7	
     8	Frame Job is free to use and its source is open. It's made by one developer, and a tip helps pay for the time to keep working on it. Tipping is voluntary, and nothing in Frame Job is locked without one.
     9	
    10	<AtAGlance
    11	  where="The green Tips button at the right end of the toolbar, and Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Tips"
    12	/>
    13	
    14	## Leave a tip
    15	
    16	Click the green **Tips** button at the right end of the editor's toolbar, after **Export…**. A small window opens, titled Tips, that says who a tip pays for.
    17	
    18	| Button | What it does |
    19	| --- | --- |
    20	| **Leave a Tip** | Opens the tips page in your browser, then closes the window. <kbd>↩</kbd> presses it. |
    21	| **Not Now** | Closes the window. <kbd>⎋</kbd> presses it, and so does the window's close button. |
    22	
    23	Frame Job takes no payment itself. The page in your browser does that, and Frame Job never learns whether you tipped.
    24	
    25	The same window opens from **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Tips**, with or without a project open. It isn't a sheet, so you can keep working with it open.
    26	
    27	## When Frame Job asks
    28	
    29	Frame Job opens the Tips window by itself rarely, and only just after an export has finished.
    30	
    31	- **The first time** comes once you've finished at least 5 exports and 30 days have passed since the first of them. If you press **Leave a Tip** before then, that counts as having been asked, and the next time is a December.
    32	- **After that**, once a year, in December. If Frame Job asked, or you pressed **Leave a Tip**, after the start of June, it skips that year's December.
    33	
    34	It appears when you close the result of an **Export…**, or when an export on the queue finishes: one you added, or one an agent or the Assistant started. It never takes the keyboard, so a key you were typing can't press one of its buttons, and it never holds up an agent's next call. If Frame Job is behind another app at that moment, the window waits there and doesn't bring Frame Job forward. Close it and it won't come back until the next time it's due.
    35	
    36	Every export that finishes counts, whoever started it: **Export…** and **Add to Queue** in the export sheet, an agent's [`export`](/mcp/export/) and the Assistant's. An export that fails or is cancelled doesn't count.
    37	
    38	Opening the window yourself and choosing **Not Now** changes nothing about when Frame Job next asks.
    39	
    40	## Turn tips off
    41	
    42	Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** and find **Tips**, the last section.
    43	
    44	| Control | What it does | Default |
    45	| --- | --- | --- |
    46	| **Show the Tips button and the yearly reminder** | Shows the green **Tips** button in the toolbar and lets Frame Job open the Tips window by itself. Untick it to stop both. | On |
    47	| **Tips** | Opens the Tips window. It's always there, whatever the box says. | |
    48	
    49	The box saves the moment you click it, and the button leaves or returns in every open editor window at once.
    50	
    51	## Good to know
    52	
    53	- Frame Job keeps the count of your exports, the date of the first one and the date it last asked in macOS's preferences for Frame Job, on your Mac only.
    54	- December is judged by your Mac's time zone.
    55	- If you export nothing in December, Frame Job doesn't ask that year.
    56	- No agent tool opens the Tips window on request or changes this setting. An agent's export finishing can bring the reminder, as yours can.
    57	- A [test copy on its own socket](/mcp/connect-a-client/#testing-a-second-copy) counts no exports and never opens the Tips window by itself.
    58	
    59	## Related
    60	
    61	- [Settings](/reference/settings/#tips)
    62	- [The editor window](/getting-started/editor-window/#toolbar)
    63	- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
    64	- [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/)
    65	- [Open source and notices](/reference/open-source/)

content.content:
## Tips — the dialog, the editor's button, the automatic ask, Settings' section and whose exports count (`tips_proof.py`, `tips_probe.swift`; nineteen mutants; spec §11 TIP-1…TIP-8)

The owner's Tips feature (2026-11-14): a small window that says who a tip pays for and opens one
web page, a green Tips button right of Export…, an ask Frame Job makes by itself on a schedule,
and a Settings section whose box turns the button and the ask off. The same day the owner
overruled one part: an export an agent or the Assistant starts counts, and the window opens after
it (TIP-4 as amended), with a proof's instance told from a person's by TIP-8. Its instrument is a
probe, which hands the code its clock, calendar, defaults, dialog, queue and instance rule, and
four instances over MCP. The feature has one `-RCDev` switch, `-RCDevTipsSuite <name>` (TIP-7),
and no dev tool: it exists so L4 and L5 can see a counted agent export on the running app without
writing the bundle's defaults domain.

    python3 tools/proof/tips_proof.py               # the probe, the tree's text, then the app over MCP
    python3 tools/proof/tips_proof.py --no-live     # without the L rows (no app)
    python3 tools/proof/tips_proof.py --mutant NAME # one of the nineteen; exit 1 when caught (rule R)

**The probe** is `tips_probe.swift` compiled as `main.swift` over `app/Sources` through
`swift_build.build`, with `default.metallib` (compiled from the tree's shaders) and `Blank.mp4`
beside it, because W1–W7 run real exports of a document made in process holding one rectangle
and no media, and a timeline with no media composes against that placeholder. Nothing reaches the
screen, a browser or a real defaults domain: activation policy `.prohibited`, every editor in a
window 20,000 pt off every display, the dialog's `open` and its two order calls as closures that
record, and the state in `ProbeDefaults`, a `UserDefaults` in memory whose every other call
traps. The one use of `UserDefaults.standard` is C3's toggle, set through the volatile argument
domain and cleared.

- **S1–S10, the schedule** (`TipsSchedule.isDue`, pure): each row a list of (state, moment,
  calendar) against a literal verdict — the two thresholds, the toggle, the December edges to the

Settings (Frame Job ▸ Settings…) has five sections, one under the other: MCP,
Assistant, Transcription, Playback and Tips. The first is where a person finds how to connect
an MCP client such as Claude Code to Frame Job (spec §11 MC-7); the second is
where they give Frame Job an Anthropic API key, choose the model for the
Assistant tab, and set how a long conversation is kept in bounds; the third is
where they give it an AssemblyAI API key, so that the Generate Captions sheet
can transcribe in the cloud instead of on this Mac; the fourth is where they
say whether Frame Job draws a window's graphics ahead while it is left alone
(spec §11 G-38); the fifth is where they turn the editor's Tips button and the
yearly reminder off, and can open the Tips window (spec §11 TIP-6).

The "MCP" section opens with its bold heading alone, with no ⓘ. Under it, two
so they play smoothly from the start; that it stops as soon as the person does
anything in Frame Job, starts again after the same wait, and keeps the
processor busy while it runs; and that the frames are held in memory, at most a
quarter of this Mac's and less when memory is short, until the window closes or
newer frames replace them.

The "Tips" section, last, opens with its bold heading alone, with no ⓘ, like
the MCP section. Under it, one sentence in 13 pt black (white in dark): "Frame
Job is free and open source, made by one developer. Tips are voluntary." Then a
ticked checkbox, "Show the Tips button and the yearly reminder", and under it a
"Tips" button (a white square button with a thin outline). Unticking the box
removes the green Tips button from every editor's toolbar at once and stops
Frame Job from opening the Tips window by itself; the section's own button is
always there and opens that window whatever the box says.

No long grey paragraph is left in the window; the MCP section's blurb is its
only paragraph, and it is black.

The window is as tall as its five sections on a screen with room for them. On a
shorter one, such as a 1440 × 900 display, it stops at the screen's visible
height and the sections scroll inside it, so the Playback row and the Tips
section are reached by scrolling. The expectations that "Background render"
and the Tips checkbox are visible assume a capture on a screen tall enough
that nothing scrolls.

(spec §11 #526 as extended by #541) the Leveler's words too: S12, T1's second scan and T2.

    python3 tools/proof/ai_docs_r2c_proof.py [--only S1,C1,…] [--app PATH] [--expect-red]
    RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/ai_docs_r2c_proof.py
    RC_PROOF_APP=<a base .app> python3 tools/proof/ai_docs_r2c_proof.py --expect-red
    python3 tools/proof/ai_docs_r2c_proof.py --only T1,T2      # make test (#556): no app, no write

The built app (`proof_app`'s choice) under a scratch home, driven over MCP, on projects built from
media made into `tools/proof/work/ai-docs-r2c/media/`: a `say`-voiced WAV (speech.wav, about 14 s)
and a 3 s 30 fps clip with sound (short3.mov, ffmpeg). `(c)` marks a CONTROL, which passes on the
base too; `(t)` marks a TREE row, which reads files rather than the app (red on eab6adf2's tree)
and is skipped by `--expect-red`; every other row is red on the frozen base app, and
`--expect-red` exits 0 only when that holds and no row failed for want of running.

The word map (spec §11 #526 as extended by #538): analyse, analysed, analysing, normalise,
normalised, normalises, normalising, recognise, recognised, recogniser, neighbour, neighbours,
grey, greys, labelled, summarise, standardised — whole words, any case. "analyses" is counted
apart, because the noun is right and only the verb changed.

The Leveler's words (#541): any `levell…` form, any case, with no word boundary (so "un-levelled"
counts), is a hit unless it is the JSON key `leveller`, which keeps its spelling. The key is told
by its CONTEXT, never by its file (`level_forms`): a string that is only the key or a path through
it (`leveller`, `audio.leveller.target_db`, `/audio/leveller/response`), or the key written as
`{leveller:`, `leveller (null or {` or in the list `gate, leveller, de_esser`.

the Generate Captions sheet):

- S2 "analyses" occurs once, in `analysis_job`'s `clips` (the base: 5).
- S3 (c) "cancelled" occurs 5 times in `tools/list`, as on the base: the status value and the

- S4 File ▸ Export…'s sheet dump holds "Loudness normalizes the" (the hint's words up to the
  dump's 200-character cap) and no map form, hidden views included.
- S5 File ▸ Generate Captions…'s sheet dump holds "The words are recognized ON THIS MAC" and no
  map form, hidden views included.
- S6 `detect_silence {clips: [a shape clip]}` notes "None of those clips plays any sound, so
  nothing was analyzed."
- S7 `normalize_clip {mode: "peak", target_lufs: -16}` is refused "… Pass mode \"loudness\" to
  normalize to a loudness."
- S8 the speech clip's `cache/loudness/<media>.*` removed, `normalize_clip {mode: "loudness"}`
  fails "Nothing could be normalized." and "is still being analyzed — its loudness has not been
  measured".
- S9 `add_transition` at a cut whose two clips show their whole file (refusal_proof.py 7b's
  setup) is refused naming "their neighbors and the overlap rule".
- S10 `render_graphic` of a module whose `interpolateColors` gets "bluish" names `cannot parse
  color "bluish"`.
- S11 (c) an h264 export, `cancel_export` at once, `export_status`: `cancelled` with the reason
  "Cancelled.".
- S12 `tools/list` holds no `levell…` form that is not the key (with the catalog's four old
  texts back: 4, in `enhance_voice`, `normalize_clip`, `set_action_end` and `set_audio`),
  `set_audio`'s text says "after the leveler", and the key `leveller` still occurs in it (a
  control inside the row: a replace that reached the key fails it).
- C4 (c) the editor's inspector captured with no capture default: `scale` equals
  `window_facts.scale` and `width_px` is points × scale rounded half away from zero, as Swift's
  `rounded()` does (a 825.5-point pane at 3× is 2,477 pixels, where Python's `round` says 2,476).
Launch 2 (`-RCDevCaptureScale 3`, which no host has):
- C1 the inspector capture answers scale 3, `width_px`/`height_px` are 3 × points (rounded), the
  dump says 3 and the PNG's IHDR holds the same size.
- C2 File ▸ Export…'s sheet the same, then `cancel_sheet`.
Launch 3 (`-RCDevCaptureScale 5`):
- C3 the log holds "RCDevCaptureScale must be 1, 2 or 3 (got \"5\"); captures keep the window's

All:

# is the publish workflow's appcast writer over a stand-in `sign_update`: no
# network, no key. `build_codecs.py --selftest` (codec-export C0) is the
# encoder build's key, reuse and digest rules, no network and no cmake; `codecs`
# first, because swift_build.py's selftest links the archives.
# `acknowledgements.py --selftest` (spec §11 PUB-10) is the third-party notices'
# generator over synthetic metadata, locks and package folders: no cargo, no network.
# `ai_docs_r2c_proof.py --only T1,T2` (#556) is the spelling scan, spec §11 #526: the
# string literals of app/Sources, core/src and graphic/src, and the site's pages,
# sidebar.mjs, features.json and README.md; its tree rows launch no app and write nothing.
# `mutant_anchors.py` (#554) reads every proof's mutant table without importing the proof
# and counts each anchor in the file it names, exactly once; `--selftest` is the reader
	python3 tools/proof/appcast.py --selftest
	python3 tools/proof/proof_defaults.py --ran assistant_lane_probe --ran assistant_prompt_probe
	python3 tools/proof/name_residue.py --selftest
	python3 tools/proof/name_residue.py
	python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --selftest
	python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py
	python3 tools/proof/ai_docs_r2c_proof.py --only T1,T2
	python3 tools/proof/mutant_anchors.py --selftest
	python3 tools/proof/mutant_anchors.py

# The Swift assistant helper's suite (agent/Tests; no network, dummy keys, nothing paid), road
def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--sources", type=Path, default=ROOT / "app/Sources")
    parser.add_argument("--mutant", choices=sorted(MUTANTS))
    parser.add_argument("--only", help="comma-separated row ids")
    parser.add_argument("--no-live", action="store_true", help="leave the L rows out")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    named = MUTANTS[args.mutant][0] if args.mutant else []
    if args.only:
        wanted = args.only.split(",")
    elif args.mutant:
        wanted = ["B0"] + named
    else:
        wanted = [row for row in ROWS if not (args.no_live and row in LIVE_ROWS)]
    unknown = [row for row in wanted if row not in ROWS]
    if unknown:
        print("unknown row " + ", ".join(unknown))
        return 2
    if args.mutant and set(wanted) & set(LIVE_ROWS):
        print("a mutant is a probe rebuild; the L rows do not run under one")
        return 2
    here = WORK / (f"mutant-{args.mutant}" if args.mutant else "tree")
    if here.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(here)
    here.mkdir(parents=True)
    sources = args.sources.resolve()
    if args.mutant:
        why = mutate(sources, args.mutant, here / "Sources")
        if why:
            print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: the control could not be performed — {why}")
            return 2
        sources = here / "Sources"

    results = {}
    not_scored = []
    probe_wanted = [row for row in wanted if row in PROBE_ROWS]
    if "B0" in wanted or probe_wanted:
        binary, why = build(sources, here)
        results["B0"] = (binary is not None, why or f"built from {sources}")
        if binary is None and args.mutant:
            print(f"B0 fail — {why}")
            print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: the control could not be performed — the copy did "
                  "not build")
            return 2
        if probe_wanted:
            if binary is None:
                for row in probe_wanted:
                    results[row] = (False, "not run: the probe did not build")
            else:
                answer, why = probe(binary, here)
                rows = (answer or {}).get("rows") or []
                for row in probe_wanted:
                    found = next((a for a in rows if a.get("id") == row), None)
                    if found is None:
                        not_scored.append(row)
                        results[row] = (False, f"no row: {why or 'the probe did not answer it'}")
                    else:
                        results[row] = (bool(found["pass"]), found["detail"])
    if "T1" in wanted:
        results["T1"] = tree_row(sources)
    if set(wanted) & set(LIVE_ROWS):
        results.update(live(wanted))

    for row in wanted:
        good, detail = results[row]
        print(f"{row} {'pass' if good else 'fail'} — {detail}")
    passed = sum(1 for row in wanted if results[row][0])
    print(f"scores: {passed}/{len(wanted)}")
    if not args.mutant:
        return 0 if passed == len(wanted) else 1
    lost = [row for row in named if row in not_scored or row not in results]
    if lost:
        print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: the control could not be performed — "
              f"{', '.join(lost)} not scored")
        return 2
    survived = [row for row in named if results[row][0]]
    if survived:
        print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: SURVIVED — {', '.join(survived)} passed")
        return 0
    print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: CAUGHT — {', '.join(named)} failed")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
def tree_row(sources):
    texts = {p.name: p.read_text() for p in sorted(sources.glob("*.swift"))}

    def files(needle):
        return sorted(name for name, text in texts.items() if needle in text)

    def count(needle):
        return sum(text.count(needle) for text in texts.values())

    facts = [
        (".exportSucceeded( is called once, in the export door",
         count(".exportSucceeded(") == 1 and files(".exportSucceeded(") == [DOOR]),
        (".follow(queueJob: is called twice, once in the export door and once in the agent's",
         count(".follow(queueJob:") == 2
         and files(".follow(queueJob:") == sorted([DOOR, AGENT_DOOR])),
        ("TipsDoors is named in the two doors' files and its own alone",
         files("TipsDoors") == sorted([DOOR, AGENT_DOOR, WINDOW])),
        (f"{SUITE_SWITCH} is spelled in {STATE} alone", files(SUITE_SWITCH) == [STATE]),
        (".takeAsk( is called in the Tips window's file alone", files(".takeAsk(") == [WINDOW]),
        (".countExport( is called in the Tips window's file alone",
         files(".countExport(") == [WINDOW]),
    ]
    detail = "; ".join(f"{name} {ok}" for name, ok in facts)
    detail += (f" (exportSucceeded in {files('.exportSucceeded(')}, follow in "
               f"{files('.follow(queueJob:')}, TipsDoors in {files('TipsDoors')})")
    return all(ok for _, ok in facts), detail


# ---- L: the app over MCP ----------------------------------------------------------

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The documentation site (`docs/site/`) against the tree. No app, no build, no network, stdlib
only; `pnpm build` in `docs/site/` is what proves the site renders and its links land.

A user-visible change has to reach the site, and nothing about the site's build notices a menu
item or an agent tool it has never heard of. These rows do:

  D1  every page has a title and a description;
  D2  the sidebar and the pages are one-to-one;
  D3  every feature in `src/data/features.json` names a page, and an anchor that page has;
  D4  every product tool in `AgentCatalog*.swift` has a heading on an `mcp/` page, and no dev tool
      (`AgentServer+DevTools.swift`) is named anywhere;
  D5  every menu item in `AppDelegate+*Menu*.swift` and `EditorViewController+GraphicMenus.swift`
      is on a reference page;
  D6  no page names something internal: a decision ID, a road map, an `rc_*` export, a source
      file, a dev launch default;
  D7  no page or data file holds a local path;
  D8  every `<Shot>` names a capture that exists in both looks;
  D9  no page uses the words `docs/site/CLAUDE.md` bans;
  D10 every tool an `AtAGlance` names is a product tool, and every step of a menu path written on
      a page is a string in `app/Sources` (`MACOS_MENU` allows what macOS draws itself), so a
      renamed menu item can't stay on the site under its old name;
  D11 the site replaced the user guide, so `docs/guide/` does not exist and no text file the gate
      hashes, whatever its suffix, outside `archive/`, `designs/adr/` and `GUIDE_ALLOWED`, links
      into it (a relative link, or a GitHub URL of this repository).

    python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py                       # the tree (make test)
    python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages a.mdx b.mdx   # those pages: D1, D6–D9
    python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --guide               # D11 alone (make gate's names)
    python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --selftest            # CONTROL + M1..M15

`--selftest` copies the site's inputs to `tools/proof/work/docs_site/` and requires the copy to
show no problem (CONTROL), then eleven mutants, each on a fresh copy, to show a problem in exactly
its row; then D11's CONTROL on a scratch root, `tools/proof/work/docs_site_guide/`, and its four
mutants, fifteen mutants in all. Exit 0 when all hold, 1 otherwise.
"""

import argparse
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", ".."))
SITE = os.path.join(ROOT, "docs", "site")
WORK = os.path.join(ROOT, "tools", "proof", "work", "docs_site")
SOURCES = os.path.join(ROOT, "app", "Sources")

# A menu's own title is not an item, and macOS writes these rows' text itself.
MENU_SKIP = {"MainMenu", "Services", "Open Recent"}

# The menus, and the steps of a menu path macOS draws or the app words as it runs: File's document
# items, Undo's name for the edit, and a Settings section's info button.
TOP_MENUS = {"File", "Edit", "Insert", "Clip", "Track", "Mark", "View", "Window", "Help",
             "Frame Job"}
MACOS_MENU = re.compile(r"^(?:Revert To|Move To…|Share|Close All|Undo .+|Redo .+|ⓘ|.+, for the key)$")
